newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Trade to feature in Clinton Australia visit.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Trade to feature in Clinton Australia visit.

text.p: Trade issues are expected to figure heavily in talks between Australian Prime Minister John Howard and U.S. President Bill Clinton here next week, Australian officials said on Thursday.

But they would not say if Howard would raise the thorny issue of a trade row over an Australian leather company's exports to the United States that has prompted Washington to complain to the World Trade Organisation (WTO).

A senior Australian official told reporters the pair would discuss bilateral trade and broader trade issues, including Clinton's trade policy for his second term in office, ahead of this month's summit of Asia-Pacific Economic Co-operation (APEC) forum leaders in the Philippines.
But asked about the dispute over an Australian trade scheme, the official said: "There are obviously one or two trade issues which are important to Australia and there are issues which are current.
"But I'm not going to say how or whether the prime minister might take those up."

The United States has launched an action against Australia's import credit scheme for automotive and textile, clothing and footwear products, complaining the programme's tax breaks provide an unfair advantage under WTO rules.
The scheme has helped Melbourne-based leather company Howe Leather gain three percent of the U.S. car leather market.
Australian industry analysts say the U.S. action threatens some A$5 billion ($4 billion) in exports and 15,000 jobs.
Australian politicians and business leaders in turn complain the United States is more restrictive than Australia.
Deputy Prime Minister and Trade Minister Tim Fischer has frequently criticised Washington for not abolishing an old U.S. law, known as the Jones Act, which bans ferry imports from foreign makers.
Clinton is due to arrive in Australia on November 19 for a brief visit before the APEC summit, including a rare address to a joint sitting of both houses of parliament.

APEC groups Australia, Brunei, Canada, Chile, China, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Japan, South Korea, Malaysia, Mexico, New Zealand, Papua New Guinea, the Philippines, Singapore, Taiwan, Thailand and the United States.
